newsitem.title: UK: Profits elude many direct insurers - report.
newsitem.headline: Profits elude many direct insurers - report.

text.p: Most direct, or tele, insurers in Europe are finding it hard to make a profit despite their success in winning business from traditional providers, Datamonitor said in a report.

"Apart from a small number of market leaders such as Direct Line, Churchill and the Dutch tele-insurer, Central Beheer, few of them actually make a profit," the management consultancy said in its report 'European Tele-insurers: A Promise Unfulfilled.'

The report said direct insurers, which bypass intermediaries and use greenfield sites, nevertheless face sizeable start-up costs in the form of marketing and information technology, while margins are low.
"To cover these costs and achieve profitability, companies need to attract a minimum number -- or critical mass -- of customers."
Datamonitor noted that few direct insurers expected to make a profit in the first five years, adding that the big, established players benefited from lower unit costs than smaller newcomers.
"Smaller operations that fail to achieve rapid growth are likely either to fold or to be absorbed by more successful competitors."

Several insurers, including Zurich, Winterthur and AGF, aim to increase European market share through their direct operations, but Datamonitor said this would not be easy in an already overcrowded market place.
"Many European markets are...already struggling to accommodate the companies that currently operate...The advent of telebroking will only further increase competition."
Telebrokers provide a quote over the telephone and perform a similar function to direct insurers, but with lower start-up costs.

"Over the next decade, teleinsurance will be highly lucrative for the leaders in the industry. Many underwriters, however...will find themselves on a telephone treadmill, and will never be able to make their teleinsurance operations profitable," said Datamonitor analyst Ferdinando Agos.
